newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine strike-busting firms have buses burnt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine strike-busting firms have buses burnt.

text.p: Unknown arsonists set fire to five buses belonging to firms in far southern Argentina that plan to defy a 36-hour general strike set to begin Thursday, local media reported.

Representatives of the three firms that own the buses met Rio Negro province officials Thursday morning to request guarantees of safety for drivers who decide to work through the strike, set to begin at midday local time/1500 GMT.
The attacks took place in the early hours Thursday and the company officials sid they interpreted the strike as a warning.

The strike is being led by the CGT union confederation, which is usually close to the governing Peronist Party. But, angry at unemployment of 17.1 percent, it is fighting President Carlos Menem's drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labor laws.
